title: Towards Probing Speech-Specific Risks in Large Multimodal Models: A Taxonomy, Benchmark, and Insights

bias_targets.methodology: Creating synthetic speech audio where identical ostensibly low-risk text is spoken by male versus female voices, and prompting Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) with Yes/No and Multiple-Choice questions to detect implicit gender stereotypes and prejudice induced by the paralinguistic cues.

Using text-to-speech systems to generate audio of identical text spoken by young versus elderly voices, and evaluating the models' ability to recognize implicit ageist stereotypes and prejudice via targeted prompting strategies.

Generating speech audio with different accents (e.g., Indian accent versus American native accent) for identical text content, and testing the models' capability to detect ethnic prejudice and stereotyping using prompt-based queries.
